facts.text: Sherwood Park began as Campbelltown in 1953, but Canada Post renamed it Sherwood Park in 1956 to avoid confusion with other towns.
Sherwood Park’s Heritage Mile preserves old landmarks like the Ottewell homestead, offering a living window into the county’s pioneer past.
Ukrainian Cultural Heritage Village in Sherwood Park brings pioneer life to life with costumed interpreters reenacting early settlers’ daily routines.
Sherwood Park sits within Alberta’s Industrial Heartland, hosting Canada’s largest hydrocarbon refining cluster.
Gallery @501, located at the Centre in the Park, rotates local, provincial, and national art exhibits every six weeks.
Sherwood Park’s historic train station lets visitors interact with artifacts like a grain elevator and general store, preserving the town’s rail legacy.
